text:
Will Cuylle has become the Rangers' utility piece, the player the New York Post says is "showcasing his Rangers flexibility with an eye on the future." He hits (89 of them in 24 games), he kills chances, and he gets to the net. Evolving-Hockey rated him 94th percentile among forwards at taking expected goals away last season.

The goals are lagging the looks. He has 6 on 8.7 expected goals (the quality of his chances), and in the last ten games just 2 on 3.7 expected. His 1.30 individual expected goals per 60 minutes is a real top-six number, up from 1.00 last season. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking backs that up: he takes a lot of shots off passes across the slot or from behind the net, the kind that go in about 25% of the time.

So the process is better than the line. The last two games (losses to Carolina and Buffalo) brought 8 shots and no goals. Our range puts him at 16 to 28 goals for the season. If the shooting catches up with the chances, his next contract gets more expensive.
